title: Half-Pro Remodeling: Homeowner Does the Easy 60%
one_liner: Fixed-price booking of only the licensed, permit-required slice of a project while homeowners or handymen do demo, prep and finish, with photo-verified handoffs.
customer: Budget-constrained homeowners with $3-15K bath, kitchen, water-heater, mini-split and electrical projects. Supply side: solo licensed plumbers and electricians who want prequalified, ready-to-work half-day jobs.
problem: Angi data shows 73% of homeowners have unstarted projects and 72% of postponers cite budget. The average project is $5,368. DIY-only fell from 50% to 39% while homeowner-plus-pro rose from 27% to 46%. Pros say they are too busy and skip small, messy, scope-uncertain jobs. Platforms sell whole jobs, so homeowners get no quotes.
solution: A catalog of standardized pro steps: rough-in for a vanity swap, shutoff valve and supply lines, gas line, water heater swap, ceiling-fan or lighting circuit, mini-split hookup, permit pull and inspection sign-off. Each comes with a homeowner checklist (nine prep steps, three photos) checked by a vision model, and a pro shows up for a fixed price to a job that is actually ready. Start only where owner-builder and licensing rules are clear.
why_now: Angi's 2026 backlog data. Credit cards rose to 30% of project payments. 62% now choose repair over replace. Contractors are capacity-constrained. Multimodal models can verify prep photos cheaply.
revenue_model: 15-20% take on the pro-step price ($300-1,500), plus materials affiliate margin from a local supply house. Pros pay nothing upfront.
non_obvious_insight: The unit of demand is not the project, it is the licensed hour. The blended-work data says homeowners do not want turnkey, they want to transfer risk only on the parts they legally or practically cannot do. Nobody sells the licensed two hours with a photo-checked handoff, and small pros love the productivity of arriving at a ready job.
first_30_days: One metro, four job types. Recruit 10 solo plumbers and electricians from local trade Facebook groups. Launch a landing page with local ads. Run 30 bookings by hand with a spreadsheet and Stripe.

title: Test-once PFAS proof registry for packaging importers
one_liner: A SKU-level registry and group-buy of accredited PFAS lab reports, so importers of the same factory's food packaging share one test and can produce an authority-ready dossier fast.
customer: EU importers, wholesalers and white-label brands of grease-resistant paper and fibre food packaging (takeaway boxes, bakery bags, burger wraps, pizza boxes, cups), plus online B2B packaging shops. Owners, purchasing or QA managers pay.
problem: Since 12 Aug 2026 the packaging regulation bans PFAS in food-contact packaging above limits (25 ppb per non-polymeric substance, 250 ppb sum, 50 ppm total PFAS), with no grandfathering for stock made earlier. Compliance guides say supplier self-declarations are not proof and that importers and producers carry the liability, with accredited-lab reports needed per packaging type. Authorities can request the technical documentation on short notice. There is no harmonised EU test method and lab capacity is finite. Each importer paying separately for the same factory's product is wasteful.
solution: A registry keyed to product specification, coating, factory and production lot. Factories, labs and importers upload accredited lab reports (cheap total organic fluorine screening first, then targeted LC-MS/MS). Other importers of the same factory and spec can match and attach the report to their own technical file. A lot-matching check and re-test reminders keep the proof valid, and an 'authority request pack' export assembles the file in one click. Group-buy: when several importers sell the same SKU, the platform pools the cost of one accredited test and negotiates volume prices with 2-3 labs. Each importer remains legally responsible, so the tool shows exactly what evidence it does and does not cover.
why_now: The ban applied on 12 Aug 2026, six weeks ago, and stock made before then cannot be sold. Labs expect demand to climb through enforcement and there is no harmonised method yet, so evidence quality varies.
revenue_model: EUR 150-400 per verified report access, EUR 25 per month per SKU for monitoring and re-test alerts, plus a 10-15% margin on group-purchased lab tests. Optional paid dossier assembly at EUR 300-600.
non_obvious_insight: Every importer treats PFAS proof as its own cost, but the object being proven is the packaging type. The same few hundred factory SKUs flow through thousands of importers, which creates network effects for a 'test once, verify per lot' registry that no consultancy or lab has an incentive to build. Evidence: guides state that 'self-declarations from suppliers do not constitute proof' and that certificates of analysis are needed per packaging type (https://www.certivo.com/blog-details/ppwr-pfas-ban-in-food-contact-packaging-what-manufacturers-must-have-ready-by-august-2026); the ban has no grandfather clause and responsibility falls on manufacturers and importers (https://www.kivo.nl/en/knowledge-base/pfas-ban-in-food-packaging-what-does-it-mean-for-your-products/); testing runs from a few hundred euros for screening to several thousand for targeted analysis, labs have limited capacity, and no harmonised EU method exists (https://pakfactory.com/blog/how-to-test-packaging-for-pfas; https://foodpackagingforum.org/news/ppwr-pfas-limits-apply-from-august-12).
first_30_days: Sign volume pricing with 2 accredited labs for TOF screening and targeted panels. Recruit 10 importers from packaging trade associations, LinkedIn groups and B2B packaging marketplaces. Ask them to list their top 20 SKUs and factories, then find overlaps between them. Run the first pooled test for the most-shared SKU at a per-importer cost far below a solo test. Publish a free 'PFAS status per SKU' lookup to attract more importers. Legal-review the shared-report disclaimer language with a food-contact lawyer.

title: AI-Run Cardiometabolic Care at ACCESS Prices
one_liner: An AI-first, pharmacist-supervised chronic-care program engineered to profit at Medicare ACCESS payment rates that break human-coach models.
customer: CMS pays it as an ACCESS participant ($360 per beneficiary per year initially, $180 follow-on, with half withheld pending outcomes). Medicare beneficiaries enroll at no cost. Later Medicare Advantage and Medicaid plans pay.
problem: ACCESS launched Jul 5, 2026 with ~150 participants. Payment works out to ~$30/month and Omada and Hinge sat out, so incumbents' cost structures don't fit. Primary care cannot titrate hypertension, lipid and prediabetes meds for millions of patients at this price.
solution: A mailed validated BP cuff and scale, voice-AI check-ins, protocolized titration of low-cost generics (ARB or CCB, statin, ezetimibe, metformin) and low-dose oral GLP-1 maintenance. Pharmacist and NP co-sign changes, with autonomous renewals only where state sandboxes allow (Utah's Jan 2026 AI renewal pilot covers 190 meds but excludes injectables and controlled substances).
why_now: ACCESS is live with rolling cohorts and a Jan 1, 2027 start. Oral GLP-1s are now first-line accessible, real-time voice AI is deployable, and a state has legally let AI renew chronic prescriptions.
revenue_model: CMS outcome-aligned payments of $360/year initial and $180/year follow-on per beneficiary. Target unit cost under ~$150/year for 50%+ margin, plus outcome-linked upside.
non_obvious_insight: At $30 per member per month the winner is whoever gets cost per member under about $12/month, which is an AI-to-pharmacist ratio problem, not a product problem. Big digital-health brands are structurally excluded.
first_30_days: Confirm the current CMS application window for the Jan 1, 2027 cohort. Meanwhile pilot 200 cash or MA patients with cheap cuff kits through a partner pharmacy, measure BP control and unit cost, and recruit a pharmacist supervisor and medical director.

title: Battery EPR Desk for E-Mobility Importers
one_liner: A retainer compliance service that registers, reports and budgets for battery EPR on behalf of small e-bike, scooter and power-station brands.
customer: E-bike, e-scooter, power-station and power-tool brand owners and importers of record selling into California and other battery-EPR states, typically $2-100M revenue with no regulatory staff.
problem: California signed SB 501 on Sept 20, 2026, creating medium-format battery EPR with a 60% recycling-efficiency floor. Thousands of small importers and marketplace sellers cannot parse who counts as the producer, how to pick or join a PRO, or what to report. Their packs also drive facility fires.
solution: Producer determination, PRO registration, automated unit and weight reporting from Shopify and Amazon data, fee budgeting, labeling artwork, take-back partnering, and a battery data sheet (chemistry, mass, removability). Recyclers want that sheet, and the evidence pack satisfies audits.
why_now: SB 501 was signed days ago, and California signed it while vetoing other bills. Existing state battery laws and the 74 catastrophic facility fires this year mean regulators and marketplaces will demand proof.
revenue_model: $6-24K per year retainer, plus 5-10% markup on pass-through PRO fees and take-back costs.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is not the famous brand but 3,000 small importers who cannot read statute. Becoming the compliance layer that marketplaces reference flips the distribution problem.
first_30_days: Build an 'Am I a producer?' quiz. Scrape marketplaces for e-mobility brands selling into California and email 300. Sign 10 for a $1.5K registration audit. Approach one marketplace's compliance team.

title: Tele-Operated Night Aides for Small Care Homes
one_liner: Metered remote-aide hours operating an off-the-shelf mobile manipulator robot in 6-16 bed residential care homes, so labor crosses borders when workers cannot.
customer: Owners of small residential care homes and assisted living homes (adult family homes, RCFEs) that run one awake overnight staffer, paying about $2,500-4,000 a month per home.
problem: Staffing is collapsing, with a 75-country visa pause, Haitian TPS loss and Wisconsin homes closing wings. One Wisconsin operator spent $100k+ on housing for overseas workers and then lost visa access. Small homes cannot buy robots or hire tech staff, and much aide time is walking, fetching and watching.
solution: Lease a wheeled mobile-manipulator (for example a Hello Robot Stretch-class unit) and pair it with remote aides, offshore or US-based. The remote aide handles night rounds, door and light tasks, supply fetching and two-way calming talk with dementia residents. The aide escalates to the on-site caregiver through a shared protocol. Do not touch medication or personal care.
why_now: Teleoperated home robots (1X NEO, Waymo-style remote centers) proved the model in 2025-26. Workers can no longer be moved, but work can. Occupancy is at a 19-year high with no new supply before 2030.
revenue_model: Monthly subscription per home covering robot lease plus a pool of remote hours. Overage billed per hour. Target unit margin of about 40% after remote-labor cost.
non_obvious_insight: Staffing rules count bodies on site, but most overnight risk is watching and fetching, which a remote human plus a modest robot can cover. The visa crackdown turns labor arbitrage into a physical-presence product.
first_30_days: Sign three care homes in one state that allow tech-augmented overnight staffing. Buy one robot and hire two remote aides. Run supervised night shifts and log fall and wandering response times as proof for the next 20 sales.

title: Mod-Approved Human Panels for Rare Audiences
one_liner: A research-recruitment service that turns Reddit's hardest-to-reach niche communities into bot-proof, mod-approved survey panels, with participants paid directly and the community getting the results back.
customer: UX and market research teams at health-tech, B2B SaaS and pharma patient-insights groups, boutique research agencies, and academic labs that need rare respondents (night-shift nurses, HVAC techs, POTS patients, first-time landlords, small-farm owners). Projects run $3k-$25k.
problem: Mainstream panels are being contaminated. A PNAS paper showed an autonomous AI survey respondent passing 99.8% of 6,000 standard attention checks. Rare-audience recruiting already costs $100-$300+ per complete and is slow. Researchers try recruiting in subreddits, but mods delete nearly every third-party survey post because of spam, data-harvesting fears, no ethics statement, no give-back, and no sample cap. Researchers get banned, and mod teams drown in survey modmail.
solution: A standardized 'research request kit': ethics and data-handling statement, incentive amount, sample cap, screener, and a commitment to post a plain-language results summary back to the community. Mods get a free Devvit intake queue with a checklist so approval takes about 60 seconds. Participants are paid directly (gift cards or PayPal), and nothing is paid to mods or communities, which respects Rule 5. Respondents can opt in to prove community tenure through user-consented OAuth (account age and history in that sub) plus a short liveness check and behavioral AI-agent detection. Buyers get a fraud-audit report with the data.
why_now: Agentic AI now beats standard survey quality checks (PNAS, late 2025), and research teams are actively looking for provably human samples. Reddit's five-community moderator cap, enforced from 31 March 2026, has thinned experienced mod teams, so requests that arrive pre-vetted and standardized are far more likely to be approved than cold modmail.
revenue_model: Per-complete pricing of $40-$150 (participant incentive $15-$60, gross margin roughly 35-45%), a $1.5k recruitment setup fee per project, annual retainers for repeat research teams, and a paid 'verified human' audit add-on.
non_obvious_insight: A mod team's approval plus demonstrable community tenure is a stronger anti-bot screen than any attention check, because aged, niche-active accounts are expensive to fake at scale and community norms punish liars. Mods say no for three fixable reasons (no results back, no data promises, no cap), so fixing those makes them say yes. The buyer's real pain isn't cost per complete but the fear that their data is silently synthetic.
first_30_days: Write the request kit and a one-page ethics template. Recruit 10 mid-size niche mod teams (10k-300k members) through mod Discords and existing goodwill, offering the intake queue free. Land 3 paid pilots from UX consultancies or academic labs at a 30% discount in exchange for case studies. Run three studies of about 100 completes each. Publish a side-by-side fraud audit against a conventional panel sample. Review Reddit's Data API commercial terms first, and keep responses collected off-platform.

title: Scam-Compound Geo-Intelligence for Compliance Teams
one_liner: A monthly geospatial register of scam compounds, built from satellite imagery and RF data, that lets exchanges and banks flag payees and merchants with a physical nexus to them.
customer: Financial-crime investigators and sanctions teams at crypto exchanges, stablecoin off-ramps, OTC desks, Asian correspondent banks and payment processors. Secondary: anti-scam consortia (for example GASA members) and the US/UK scam-center task forces that agreed on 4 Sept 2026 to coordinate takedowns.
problem: Chainalysis puts 2025 scam revenue near $17B, with AI-enabled operations averaging $3.2M versus $719K, and US investment fraud alone hit $8.65B. On-chain tools label wallets but nobody maps the physical compounds (Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, now spreading) to counterparties. Compounds relocate after raids, and enforcement and sanctions need evidence of place, not just of transactions.
solution: A register of suspected compounds and displacement corridors built from optical and SAR change detection (perimeter walls, dormitory blocks, razor-wire, rooftop dish counts, nighttime lights) plus purchased RF-geolocation data on satellite-terminal uplinks, cross-referenced to corporate registries and Telegram guarantee marketplaces. Delivered as a risk API and CSV: 'this payee's declared address, IP cluster or KYC address is within X km of a flagged compound', with analyst-reviewed confidence tiers and evidence packets for suspicious-activity reports. Also a relocation forecast near border economic zones.
why_now: The US and UK agreed on 4 Sept 2026 to coordinate scam-center takedowns, and 2025 sanctions on the Prince Group showed enforcement appetite. Commercial revisit rates and cheap SAR now make monthly monitoring affordable. Reporting has documented satellite-internet terminals at compounds, giving them an RF and imagery signature.
revenue_model: $3-8K per compound-exposure assessment for investigations teams and $10-25K per month for the risk feed and API. Consortium data-sharing licences later.
non_obvious_insight: On-chain analytics see money but not place, and compounds are physically huge, slow to build and hard to hide, unlike wallets. They sit in a gap between defense-intel EO buyers and commercial AML, so no one serves them. Compliance teams need geographic-nexus evidence to justify de-risking specific corridors instead of blanket bans, and a place-based register gives regulators something to point to.
first_30_days: Validate signatures on known compounds (KK Park, Shwe Kokko, Sihanoukville, Golden Triangle zone) with Sentinel-1 and 2 plus $5-10K of commercial imagery credit. Publish a free 'Compound Atlas' of 30 sites with human-reviewed confidence tiers. Pitch 5 exchange investigations heads and one anti-scam NGO consortium, and sell 2-3 paid assessments.

title: Flash-Heated Graphite Restoration From Anode Scrap
one_liner: Use flash Joule heating to restore spent and scrap anode graphite to usable grade in seconds, giving US anode makers a domestic, non-Chinese feedstock.
customer: US anode makers and cell manufacturers needing non-Chinese graphite (buyers), and cell-plant scrap managers (feedstock sellers).
problem: Graphite is a large share of black-mass weight, and hydromet recyclers typically treat it as waste. China dominates anode graphite, has tightened graphite export licensing, and the US has almost no domestic supply.
solution: A pulsed reactor (flash Joule heating, from academic work at Rice) purifies and re-graphitizes anode scrap at about 3000 K in seconds, using far less energy than conventional graphitization furnaces. The first product is a 100 kg/day pilot line producing qualification samples, with early sales into non-battery markets while battery-grade qualification proceeds.
why_now: Chinese graphite controls, US trade remedies, and rising domestic cell-plant scrap volumes all arrived in the last two years, and flash processing moved from lab papers to pilots.
revenue_model: Tolling or per-kg sale priced against imported anode-grade graphite, plus grants and offtake advance payments.
non_obvious_insight: Graphite is the one battery material that recycling plants throw away while the US has essentially no domestic supply.
first_30_days: License or build a bench flash reactor. Collect 500 kg of anode scrap from a cell-plant scrapper. Produce samples and send to 3 anode makers or national labs for coin-cell testing. File for DOE or DoD SBIR funding.

title: Cloud-Bricking Escrow for Hardware Brands
one_liner: A neutral escrow-and-standby service that holds a hardware brand's cloud backend and local-mode firmware, and takes over the moment the cloud vendor fails.
customer: Consumer-hardware brands that outsource their cloud or app to an ODM or startup: private-label and licensed smart-home, router, EV-charger, pet-tech and e-bike brands. Retailers and insurers are secondary buyers.
problem: When a small backend vendor dies, the brand that sold the device takes the blame. Motorola-branded routers stopped being manageable when the MotoSync+ app failed. Play Store reviews say a third-party backend host's licence expired and the host ended operations ('Server Licence Expired'). Users report months without a fix. Spotify Car Thing became 'a $200 hardware turned into e-waste overnight.' An HN commenter estimated $300k-600k to open-source a single project, so afterthought rescue is unaffordable.
solution: For a flat annual fee, the brand deposits its backend container images and infrastructure-as-code, sealed secrets, signed 'local mode' firmware or companion-app builds, and device protocol docs. The operator monitors cloud health, domain and cert expiry, app-store status and vendor solvency signals. On a trigger it either runs the backend on standby infrastructure (pay-per-device) or releases the local-mode build. Brands that certify get an 'Afterlife Ready' mark for retail listings and regulator conversations.
why_now: EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations began on 11 Sept 2026, with full manufacturer obligations from 11 Dec 2027 and lifecycle handling required. Startup shutdowns are running at a high rate: 14.4% of H1 2026 shutdowns were AI companies with a median age of 2.3 years and a median $30k cash at closure. Recent bricking cases (Motorola routers in Jun 2026, Nest thermostats, Kodak Pulse frames, Samsung fridges in Sept 2026) are fresh in retailers' minds.
revenue_model: $5-25k/yr escrow subscription per brand, plus $0.10-0.50/device/month for hot standby and a per-incident recovery fee. Certification audits are a later add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The liability chain runs from a dead vendor through the brand to the customer, and existing escrow (software licence escrow, to my knowledge) is not built for live device fleets. Evidence: the Motorola router thread (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48425611, 238 points) traces the outage to a third-party server licence expiring after the host company ended operations. The 'when hardware goes EOL' essay (https://www.marcia.no/words/eol; HN discussion at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46609492, 403 points) lists Nest, Car Thing and Kodak Pulse. It quotes the $300k-600k open-sourcing estimate and community workarounds (OpenWRT, 'No Longer Evil'). The EU CRA page (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act) sets the 11 Sept 2026 and 11 Dec 2027 dates. The buyer is the brand, not the consumer, and the fee has to be cheaper than a single recall.
first_30_days: Week 1: build a free 'BackendWatch' monitor that pings a brand's cloud endpoints, cert expiry and domain renewals. Week 2: cold-email 50 licensed-brand and private-label hardware companies, and Kickstarter-scale hardware founders. Weeks 3-4: sign 3 design partners on a $2.5k pilot escrow. Write the trigger contract with a startup-insolvency lawyer.

title: Indonesia Halal Rescue for Food Exporters
one_liner: A fast-track service that gets mid-size food, supplement and cosmetics exporters registered and documented under Indonesia's mandatory halal regime, then keeps them compliant.
customer: Mid-size US, EU and Australian exporters and their Indonesian importers, plus halal certifiers who white-label the work.
problem: Halal certification becomes mandatory for imported food, beverages, cosmetics and supplements on 17 Oct 2026, with enforcement from 18 Oct. The authority says no extensions, certification takes 3-6 months, and USDA FAS (Sept 2026) flags roughly $2.5B of US ag exports affected. Many mid-size firms treat halal as a marketing label and have not started.
solution: A gap analysis, supplier halal-declaration collection, matching to recognized foreign halal bodies, registration filing, and label and claim review. A software ledger tracks every ingredient and supplier certificate across SKUs and alerts on expiry, which also serves kosher and EU documentation needs.
why_now: The cliff is three weeks away and the lead time exceeds that, so late movers face shipment holds. After the deadline the work shifts to cure (relabeling, re-filing, clearing stuck shipments), which is recurring.
revenue_model: $4-15k per SKU-family project plus $500-2k/month monitoring, and certifier white-label fees.
non_obvious_insight: Halal has become a customs gate rather than a marketing certificate, so budgets come from logistics and compliance, not brand. The ingredient-and-supplier documentation ledger is reusable across regimes.
first_30_days: Email and LinkedIn outreach to 300 exporters from USDA export directories and state trade offices, offering a $750 48-hour readiness check. Partner with 1-2 recognized halal bodies and prioritize firms with shipments already in transit.

title: Manufactured-Home Replacement With Salvage Financing
one_liner: A turnkey 'old home out, new home in' program for manufactured-home communities: hazmat survey, salvage and teardown of pre-1976 units, pad prep, then set-and-hookup crews for new factory-built homes, with scrap and reuse value helping finance the job.
customer: Manufactured-home community owners and resident-owned communities replacing derelict units, state and nonprofit replacement programs, and chattel lenders.
problem: Old manufactured homes are a huge stock of unsubsidized affordable housing, but many are at end of life. Removing one costs thousands (asbestos survey, hazmat, disposal) and takes weeks. Even as factory-built homes get cheaper, foundations, utility hookups, set crews and local financing stay local and human. The July 2026 ROAD to Housing Act killed the steel chassis rule (about $10K or 10% of unit cost), but HUD has yet to publish the new standards.
solution: A fixed-price 'decommission and pad-ready in 10 days' package: survey, harvest steel frame, axles, aluminum, copper and appliances, and route scrap and hazmat properly. Then a set-and-hookup crew for the new home, plus a lender referral and a trade-in credit that offsets the down payment. Park owners buy the program to upgrade lots.
why_now: ROAD to Housing Act (Jul 11, 2026) makes factory-built housing cheaper and HUD's standards are imminent. Tariffs raise steel and material costs, site-crew scarcity is acute, and PE-owned parks want faster unit turnover.
revenue_model: Fixed fee of roughly $6-12K per replacement (salvage revenue offsets perhaps a fifth to a third of removal cost); lender and dealer referral fees; set-crew margin later.
non_obvious_insight: The replacement bottleneck is not the factory but the exit of the old unit. Salvage and hazmat know-how turn a cost into a program, and a trade-in credit is what makes chattel financing pencil for the resident.
first_30_days: Approach 5 park owners or resident-owned co-ops with 5-20 derelict homes each. Price a pilot batch of 10 homes. Run asbestos surveys, take scrap to yards and document real per-home cost and cycle time. Use the results to sign the first paid batch and a lender partner.

title: 48-Hour Takedown Desk for Small Platforms
one_liner: A hosted notice-and-removal service that lets small user-content platforms meet the TAKE IT DOWN Act's 48-hour clock while filtering out weaponized false claims.
customer: Small and mid-size platforms hosting user content: niche forums, community and chat servers, creator and fan-content sites, marketplaces with seller photos, dating apps, and indie AI image and video generators. They pay $99-$2,000/month.
problem: Since 19 May 2026, covered platforms must run a removal process and take down non-consensual intimate imagery, including deepfakes and known identical copies, within 48 hours of a valid request. The FTC is enforcing, has sent warning letters to a dozen sites of varying sizes and can seek penalties above $50k per violation. Small teams cannot staff weekends or nights. The statute has no counter-notice or penalty for false claims, so bad-faith takedown floods by rivals or harassers are a real censorship tool.
solution: A drop-in intake page, API and email alias. Requesters are identity-verified and their signed statement is captured. Trained reviewers work 24/7 with a 4-hour internal target. Hash and perceptual matching (including StopNCII) finds copies across the customer's site. The desk executes removals, logs evidence and produces a monthly FTC-ready compliance report. A shared claimant-reputation graph flags serial or coordinated false claimants across customers, with configurable reinstatement policies.
why_now: Enforcement is live and visibly reaching small sites. AI image generators multiply NCII volume. Small platforms that could ignore trust and safety until now have a hard federal clock.
revenue_model: Subscription tiered by monthly active users and case volume, plus a per-case fee above quota. Enterprise plans for AI image and video generators, and an add-on for FTC inquiry support.
non_obvious_insight: Detection is not the scarce resource, since StopNCII and hashing already exist. The scarce resources are accountable human judgment on a 48-hour clock and cross-platform intelligence on abusive claimants, which only a shared vendor can see. The law's missing abuse safeguard is the product.
first_30_days: Build intake and workflow on Retool or Airtable with 6 ex-trust-and-safety reviewers across two time zones. Contact 100 small platforms found via FTC warning-letter coverage and forum and community host lists, offering a 30-day free pilot. Publish a free compliance checklist for lead capture, then charge $199/month from the second month.

title: Zero-Return Tax Desks Inside POS Agent Shops
one_liner: Turn trusted POS agent shops into walk-in compliance desks that get informal traders their TIN and filed small-company returns before the penalties bite.
customer: Informal and micro-traders and small registered businesses (turnover under about N100m) who need to file to claim the 0% small-company rate; POS agents who earn a revenue share; principals (banks and MFBs) who want stickier merchants.
problem: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 the 0% small-company exemption (turnover about N100m or less and fixed assets under about N250m) is not automatic. You still need a TIN, records and an annual return even when tax due is zero. Filing penalties are now N100k in month one plus N50k per month after. E-invoicing reaches medium taxpayers from July 2026 and small ones from July 2027. Most shop owners are terrified of 'tax people', do not own a smartphone workflow, and cannot afford an accountant at N50-150k. Agents already see their shop's real turnover every day but never use it.
solution: A shop-counter service where the agent collects CAC, NIN and basic details on a tablet, and the platform pre-fills the TIN check and zero or small-company return using the shop's actual bank and POS statement history, with AI extraction from the pictures. A partner chartered accountant or tax practitioner reviews and signs. Recurring layer: monthly bookkeeping and a reminder feed. Later, e-invoice readiness (NRS Merchant Buyer Solution onboarding) for those crossing the next thresholds.
why_now: NTA 2025 and the Tax Administration Act took effect on 1 January 2026, with steep new late-filing penalties. The first e-invoicing go-live dates (July 2026 for medium taxpayers, July 2027 for emerging ones) are here. CBN's April 2026 single-principal rule has made agents look for non-banking revenue that keeps customers walking in. LLM extraction from photos and PDF statements is finally cheap and accurate.
revenue_model: About N7,500-15,000 per annual return, with 30-40% going to the agent. A N2,000-3,000 per month bookkeeping and reminder subscription. Referral fees from principals and accountants. Enterprise deals to give principals a white-label tax-desk feature for their agent networks.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is trust and fear, not software, and the person who has it is the agent who has known the trader for five years. Agents also hold the one thing no tax app has: 12-24 months of a shop's real transaction history. Small-company status is a 'file to be free' product, not a 'pay tax' product, so the pitch to a trader is saving a N100k fine, not helping the government.
first_30_days: Partner with one ICAN/ANAN/CITN-registered accountant who reviews and signs. Recruit 30 agents in one Lagos market cluster (for example Ikeja or Yaba) from agent WhatsApp groups. Run a 'file before the fines' campaign at N5,000 introductory price. Aim for 300 filings in 30 days, hand-checked, and document the objection patterns and the paperwork that trips people up.

title: FTC Review-Rule Audits for Franchisors
one_liner: Fixed-fee audits that find review gating, incentivised reviews and insider reviews across a franchisor's or dealer group's locations, and in the reputation vendors doing it for them.
customer: General counsel and marketing VPs at franchisors and multi-location operators (auto dealer groups, dental support organisations, home-services and fitness franchises), with reputation-management agencies as channel partners.
problem: The FTC Consumer Review Rule bans review gating, sentiment-conditional incentives, suppression and undisclosed insider reviews, with civil penalties of up to $53,088 per violation. The FTC sent 10 warning letters in Dec 2025 and obtained a $4M order (partly suspended) in July 2026. Local operators often use review-request software that quietly routes unhappy customers away from public sites, and franchisors are exposed to franchisee behaviour.
solution: A 'Rule Ready' audit. Scan Google, Yelp, Facebook and vertical sites across all locations for suspicious bursts, employee reviews and incentive language. Mystery-shop vendors' review-request flows (does a 2-star responder get diverted from Google?). Deliver a risk-ranked location report and remediation playbook, then quarterly monitoring and a vendor certification for compliant review-request software.
why_now: Warning letters (Dec 2025), the first orders (July 2026) and law-firm commentary in mid-2026 show an enforcement pattern taking shape, and Italy's Mar 2026 Trustpilot fine shows the referee itself can be penalised.
revenue_model: $5-25k per audit scaled by location count, $2-8k per month monitoring, and certification fees from review-software vendors.
non_obvious_insight: Liability sits with the buyer of reputation software, not the vendor, and those vendors' flows were designed when gating was legal. The money follows the risk to the franchisor's general counsel.
first_30_days: Pick one vertical, either dental support organisations or auto dealer groups. Cold-email 40 general counsel with a free three-location sample audit. Build scanners on public review data and line up two law firms as referral partners.

title: Last Day Co: Small Business Wind-Down
one_liner: A flat-fee retirement service for owners who do not want to sell, just stop: legal wind-down, lease exit, records custody, customer-list handoff and a proper last day.
customer: Retiring owners of solo and micro businesses with $100k to $2M in revenue. Start with regulated solo practices (therapists, small medical or dental practices, solo attorneys, CPAs) where closing duties create urgency, then salons, restaurants and contractors.
problem: McKinsey estimates baby boomers run as many as 6M small and midsize US businesses, with roughly 2.3M to 3M expected to transition ownership this decade, yet only about 54% of owners have a succession plan and about a third of owners over 50 say they cannot find a buyer. Brokers are paid only on sales and skip tiny firms, so most simply shut. That leaves leases, personal guarantees, client records, final payroll and taxes, licenses and customers stranded.
solution: A productized 90-day closure: state and local filings and final taxes through a partner CPA, lease exit negotiation (buyout or assignment, limiting the personal guarantee), equipment and inventory liquidation, and a records-custody service where Last Day Co acts as professional custodian for 7 to 10 years with client notice and a release process. It also brokers the customer list or goodwill to a vetted local competitor, with a fee to the owner. It closes with a last-day package: customer letter, farewell event, staff reference packets.
why_now: Boomers are now roughly 62 to 80, so closures are rising toward the McKinsey-projected peak. LLMs make state-specific closure checklists, notices and letters cheap to produce accurately. Remote records custody removes the need for a physical archive.
revenue_model: A $2,500 to $9,000 flat wind-down fee. Records custody at $25 to $75 per month or a prepaid $1,500 for 7 years. A goodwill-handoff success fee of 10% to 20% of what the acquirer pays. A 10% to 15% liquidation commission.
non_obvious_insight: Brokers sell, and nobody closes. Most owners do not want a sale process, they want to stop, so the real product is permission and completion with liability handled. Custodianship for regulated practices is near-zero-churn recurring revenue, and the customer list is the only asset that survives a closure, so a warm handoff to a neighboring competitor is where the money is.
first_30_days: Pick solo therapists and solo attorneys in one state. With a local attorney and CPA, write the state-specific 'professional will and closure' playbook. Sell the $299 professional will plus closure plan through the state association newsletter and LinkedIn. Do three discounted pilot closures end to end, build a list of local acquirers for goodwill handoffs, and document each step as a repeatable checklist.

title: Drive-By Lawsuit Shield for Marketing Stacks
one_liner: Scan and fix the text, website and review flows that trigger serial-plaintiff demand letters, and back it with a response pack.
customer: Local-service SMBs and small multi-location brands, sold mostly through local marketing agencies and agency resellers on GoHighLevel, Wix and Squarespace.
problem: Serial-plaintiff waves target small firms: text-message consent and quiet-hours claims, website accessibility claims, wiretap claims over chat widgets and tracking pixels, and the FTC's fake-and-gated-review rule (prior knowledge on the rules). Demands of $5-25k get settled blind. AI-generated marketing raises exposure: 83% of AI-using small firms use AI for writing or marketing.
solution: A scanner checks known triggers: SMS consent capture and state quiet hours, trackers and chat widgets without consent banners, basic accessibility failures, review-gating flows and unsubstantiated claims. It applies or guides fixes, keeps a provenance-stamped consent ledger, and provides a demand-letter response pack via a partner law firm. Defense-cost coverage can be added through an MGA.
why_now: SMBs are now running automated texting, AI-written content and review requests, and small businesses lack legal capacity to evaluate demands.
revenue_model: $19-49 per site or number per month, $499 per response pack, plus a share of insurance premiums.
non_obvious_insight: The vendor who sells the marketing tool never gets sued, but the owner does, and the agency is liable to its client. The buyer of protection is the agency reseller, not the owner.
first_30_days: Build scanners for three triggers and run free scans on 500 local sites. Sell reports to 10 agencies and sign a law-firm partner for the response pack.

title: Co-op Childcare Kits That Also Make Parent Friends
one_liner: Modern rails (licensing map, insurance, shift scheduling, lead-teacher placement) that let 12-20 neighbor families launch a parent-participation preschool or aftercare co-op in a few months, cutting tuition and curing parent isolation at the same time.
customer: Groups of 10-20 families in childcare deserts: new-parent groups, neighborhood and church parent groups, remote-work households, employer resource groups. Later: employers and HOAs that sponsor co-ops.
problem: Childcare averages $13,128 a year and the labor inside that price is the reason. Parents are lonely (friendship is now a measured health metric), and post-2020 new parents often have few local friends. Parent co-ops once made childcare 30-50% cheaper, but they withered because launching one requires legal, licensing, insurance and payroll expertise that volunteer boards lack.
solution: 'Co-op OS': a state-by-state navigator showing where parent-participation programs are exempt or lightly licensed (verify per state), template bylaws, an insurance bundle (general liability plus abuse-and-molestation), background checks and mandated-reporter training, a shift scheduler that assigns parent duty days and keeps a credit ledger, payroll for one paid lead teacher, and a lead-teacher matching service for displaced educators. Friendship is designed in: monthly parent-only dinners, a crisis buddy system and meal trains.
why_now: Dependent-care FSAs now reach $7,500 and the 45F credit lets sponsoring employers offset 40-50% of childcare costs. Hybrid schedules and AI-driven job churn have left many parents with flexible hours to trade for tuition. Parents are already organizing collectively on phones and schools, so collective action is normalized.
revenue_model: About $1,500 setup, $149/mo per co-op for software and payroll, insurance commissions, a lead-teacher placement fee of about $2,000, and employer sponsorship of co-op slots.
non_obvious_insight: Time is the new money. Childcare is expensive because it is labor, and co-ops swap parent hours for tuition. Nobody does it because of coordination and compliance, not desire. Parent friendship is the retention engine, not a nice-to-have, and lonely parents recruit each other for you.
first_30_days: Pick two states with clear parent-participation rules. Recruit 3 existing neighbor or parent Facebook groups into a 4-week 'Co-op Launch Sprint' with a $299 deposit per family. Engage an early-childhood attorney for templates and an insurance MGA for the bundle. Place one lead teacher and aim to have three co-ops running by January 2027.

title: Revenue Recovery From Blocked Shopping Agents
one_liner: Synthetic agent shoppers try to buy from your store every night, find where bot defenses and checkout kill legitimate agent orders, and you pay a cut of the sales recovered.
customer: Mid-market e-commerce merchants ($5M-$200M GMV) on Shopify Plus, BigCommerce or Adobe Commerce with aggressive bot, WAF and fraud settings, reached through their agencies and fraud vendors.
problem: Insiders think the bottleneck is protocol adoption (ACP vs UCP vs AP2). The measurable leak is simpler. Agent usage is about 62% at comparison but only about 23% at checkout. Fraud and bot systems built for humans misclassify agent traffic (Chargebacks911 warns of a false-decline problem). CAPTCHAs, SMS one-time codes and 3DS challenges kill legitimate agent orders, and the lost sale looks like a bounce, so no dashboard shows it.
solution: Run real agent stacks (ChatGPT agent mode, Comet, Gemini, open-source browser agents, plus ACP/UCP/AP2 clients) through scripted purchase journeys on the live store with test cards. Log the exact failure point: challenge page, WAF rule, OTP step, stale feed, price mismatch. Deliver a weekly fix list (allowlist verified agent signatures, rule changes, checkout patches), then re-test to prove recovery.
why_now: Bots now outnumber humans. Stores that blocked AI bots in 2024 are undoing it, and the Ninth Circuit ruling makes user-directed agents legitimate visitors. Five competing checkout protocols make failure modes hard to see.
revenue_model: $2-5k fixed audit plus 5-10% of attributable recovered agent revenue for 12 months, or $500-$2k/month monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: A performance-fee audit is easy to buy because the merchant risks nothing. The proof is measurable (before and after test purchases), and the data becomes a benchmark of which defenses block which agents.
first_30_days: Build the harness with 3 agent stacks and 5 common checkout and WAF patterns. Offer 10 free audits to Shopify agencies who can resell. Convert the first 3 leaks worth over $5k per month into revenue-share contracts.

title: Appeal Kits for Musicians Wrongly Flagged as AI
one_liner: A DAW-side watcher that quietly notarizes your project history, so a wrongful 'AI' flag becomes a one-click appeal instead of a lost royalty stream.
customer: Independent producers and singer-songwriters releasing 5-50 tracks a year on TIDAL, Deezer, Spotify and Bandcamp, plus small labels and distributor support desks that have to rule on flagged tracks.
problem: Platforms now punish fully-AI tracks: TIDAL demonetizes them (Jul 15, 2026), Spotify excludes AI-persona profiles from recommendations (Aug 11), and Bandcamp banned AI music outright (Jan 14). Detectors are probabilistic, and with AI above 50% of Deezer uploads, thresholds will tighten and false positives will grow (my inference). A wrongly flagged human has no evidence and no appeal format. The free verified-artist badges do nothing for someone already flagged.
solution: A background agent for Ableton, Logic, Reaper and FL Studio (Ableton .als files are gzipped XML, so they diff cleanly) that hashes project files, stems, plugin chains and automation over time. It anchors the hashes to a public timestamp log and renders a shareable 'Session Timeline' page. One click exports an appeal packet formatted for each platform's dispute flow, with a verify link that distributors can check. Artists choose what to reveal and never upload raw sessions.
why_now: Enforcement went live in a six-month burst (Bandcamp Jan 2026, TIDAL Jul 15, Spotify Aug 11), so 'flagged as AI' now costs money and reach rather than a label. Detection is increasingly automated and at volume. Nobody has built the defendant's side of the process.
revenue_model: $9/month artist plan, $49 per notarized appeal packet for non-subscribers, $500-2,000/month label plans, and a per-verification API fee from distributors that want to clear flagged-track disputes faster.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody pays for proof-of-human in advance, because the badge is free. They pay at the moment of dispute. Sell the evidence, like a dashcam that is only valued after the crash, and not the badge.
first_30_days: Weeks 1-2: build a project-file watcher for Ableton and Reaper with a hosted timeline page. Weeks 3-4: recruit 30 producers from r/WeAreTheMusicMakers and producer Discords, and DM artists who have posted about false AI flags. Offer a free install and charge only for the first appeal packet. Pitch two distributor support leads on accepting the verify link.

title: Old Job Kits for Dementia Sundown Hours
one_liner: A monthly subscription of dignified, occupation-matched 'work' boxes, such as a retired bookkeeper's ledger and receipts or a retired mechanic's hardware bench, that calm sundowning better than puzzles or toys. Aides earn referral commissions.
customer: Adult children caring for a parent with moderate dementia at home (about $34-44 per month), plus adult day programs and memory care activity directors who buy in bulk. The family pays.
problem: From 4 to 7pm many dementia patients get restless, pace and get aggressive. Families use the TV, memory games or, worse, sedatives. Toys and puzzles marketed to dementia patients often insult them; they toss the plush or refuse the coloring book. What actually calms most patients is purposeful work related to the life they used to have: the retired accountant sorting receipts, the teacher grading papers, the seamstress matching buttons, the waiter folding napkins, the farmer sorting seeds.
solution: Family fills out a 3-minute 'what did they do for work?' intake. Each month a box ships with real, adult-looking, safe materials for that career. Examples are a bookkeeper's ledger, adding-machine paper, a rubber stamp and pre-sorted stacks. A teacher gets a stack of old spelling tests with a red pen and gold stars. A mechanic gets large washers and nuts on a workbench tray. Nothing sharp, small or childlike. A card gives the aide or family a 30-second 'handoff line' ('the boss needs these sorted before five'). Aides get a personal referral code and 20 percent commission.
why_now: CMS's push to reduce antipsychotic use in dementia and its GUIDE dementia care model (live since July 2024, with caregiver education and respite requirements) push practices toward cheap non-drug behavior tools. Short-form video is a free channel, since a grandfather 'clocking in' to sort receipts is deeply shareable. Families are stretched by cuts to home care hours and turn to anything that buys them a calm evening.
revenue_model: $34-44 per month subscription with quarterly rotation. Bulk B2B orders of $250 per month per adult day or memory care program. 20 percent referral commissions to aides and care managers. Upsell to 'career library' add-ons and licensed professional-uniform accessories.
non_obvious_insight: The trick is not stimulation but purpose, and it must look like a real job, because anything that looks like a child's toy is rejected as an insult. Also, families ask their aide what to buy, and aides are the most trusted product recommenders in the house, yet no brand has ever paid them. Paying aides a commission creates a distribution channel no ad budget can match and quietly raises their income.
first_30_days: Build 6 career kits (bookkeeper, teacher, mechanic, seamstress, waiter, nurse) for under $18 each from restaurant-supply, office and hardware stores. Film 15 TikTok and Instagram clips with permission from families. Post in three large caregiver Facebook groups and offer 30 free kits in exchange for video testimonials. Give 20 aides referral codes. Sign up 3 local adult day centers for a $250 monthly pilot. Aim for 50 paying subscribers by day 60.

title: SpaceX Exposure Verification Desk for Advisors
one_liner: A due-diligence service that tells advisors and retail investors whether a 'SpaceX exposure' SPV actually holds anything, and flags impersonation and deepfake endorsements timed to launch and IPO news.
customer: Registered investment advisers, family offices, broker-dealer compliance teams and private-bank due-diligence desks being pitched SPVs and notes marketed as SpaceX or Starlink exposure. Secondary: sophisticated retail via a subscription.
problem: Demand for SpaceX exposure is intense (Starlink about 12M subscribers, $11.4B 2025 revenue, Starship reached orbit on 28 Sept 2026), but shares are transfer-restricted, so anything offered is indirect: SPVs of SPVs with stacked fees, sold over LinkedIn, WhatsApp and Telegram, some holding nothing. Deepfake Musk endorsements and fake launch livestreams add a scam layer. Lumpy events such as the 16 Sept 2026 Valor distribution add confusion about what is real.
solution: (1) Map every SPV using SpaceX or Starlink naming from SEC Form D and adviser filings, with sponsor history, fee stacks and upstream fund lineage. (2) Holdings attestation by obtaining custodian, transfer agent or upstream-fund confirmation. (3) Compare marketing claims against issuer transfer restrictions and last known tender pricing. (4) A red-flag score (offshore layers, unlicensed sellers, cloned domains) and an alert feed on new offerings and impersonation around launch days and any listing.
why_now: IPO speculation, the Valor stock distribution on 16 Sept 2026, Starship's orbital flight and a record Golden Dome and launch boom are all feeding retail FOMO. Scam economics are inverting (tools cost about $50 while average payments rose 253%) and AI deepfakes are cheap. If a listing happens, the desk pivots to lock-up and SPV-unwind verification, so it does not depend on one date.
revenue_model: $750-2,500 per SPV verification report, $499 per month for adviser subscriptions with alerts, and enterprise seats for compliance teams. Later expansion to other hot pre-IPO space names.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not access to SpaceX but the truth about what an SPV holds. The key facts (Form D filings, fee layers, issuer restrictions) are public and cheap to analyze, yet every hype cycle mints exposure products faster than compliance staff can diligence. Buyers pay for a signed opinion that gives them cover to say no.
first_30_days: Scrape EDGAR for SpaceX and Starlink SPV names and publish an 'SPV Layer Map' with fee stacks. Send it to 200 RIAs and compliance officers. Offer 3 free verifications, then sell the next ones at $1,500. Set up domain-impersonation monitoring keyed to launch dates. Position as research and diligence, not investment advice.

title: Refundable-Deposit Demand Proof for Indie Hardware
one_liner: A hosted reservation page that lets small hardware creators collect refundable $20-$50 deposits at tiered locked prices, giving them price-elasticity data and a demand certificate before they commit to a campaign or a factory MOQ.
customer: First- and second-time hardware and game creators planning a Kickstarter or Indiegogo launch, plus the small factories and pledge-manager agencies that advise them. Payer is the creator.
problem: Kickstarter median funding is $7,060 versus a $64,567 average, and Indiegogo's top performers all 'arrived with an audience already built.' Small creators have followers but no proof anyone will pay, so they either launch blind or over-order inventory.
solution: A Stripe Connect-based landing page where each deposit charges the creator's own account (no funds held by us) and is refunded on request. Visitors choose among three locked-in price tiers (A/B-testing price), and a referral queue rewards sharing. The dashboard shows deposit count by country, price-tier elasticity and expected launch-day conversion. A 'demand certificate' PDF can be handed to factories negotiating MOQ or to lenders offering inventory financing. Deposits convert with one click to day-one pledges on launch.
why_now: Big brands proved the pattern in 2025-26. eufyMake ran a $50 deposit to lock a $1,499 price before its April 2025 Kickstarter and raised over $10M in 14 hours. Creality's refundable $50 deposit unlocked a $649 VIP price for its filament maker, and the goal was hit in about 16.5 minutes. Meanwhile Indiegogo retired Flexible Funding in October 2025, so both platforms are all-or-nothing and the cost of launching without proof is higher.
revenue_model: $299 setup plus 1.5% of deposits processed, a $999 launch-readiness package (demand certificate, pricing test, launch-day email sequence), and $49/mo for post-launch late-pledge and pre-order pages.
non_obvious_insight: The most successful launches of 2025-26 did not start on Kickstarter. They started with money-backed waitlists. eufyMake opened a $50 deposit pre-order scheme to lock a $1,499 price ahead of the April 29 Kickstarter (https://www.notebookcheck.net/Anker-EufyMake-E1-UV-printer-Pre-order-deposit-scheme-now-open.999622.0.html) and then raised $46.76M from 17,822 backers (https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/3d-printer-breaks-kickstarter-record-raises-44m/493857). Creality took $50 refundable deposits for VIP $649 pricing on the M1 (https://makers101.com/creality-filament-maker-m1-shredder-r1-live-tracker/). Kickstarter's own pre-launch page only collects follows, and the ecosystem is top-heavy (median $7,060 vs average $64,567, and 'all Indiegogo top performers arrived with an audience', https://www.tcf.team/blog/q1-2026-crowdfunding-report). A deposit is a far stronger demand signal than a follower, and small creators have no tool to run one, no way to test three price points, and no artefact factories will trust.
first_30_days: Build the landing page and Stripe Connect flow in 2 weeks. Pitch 10 creators with live 'coming soon' pages on Kickstarter, offering a free pilot in exchange for a case study. Run a $20-$50 deposit test with one creator (target 150+ deposits) and document the elasticity result. Publish the case study on r/Kickstarter, BackerKit-focused groups and crowdfunding Discords, then charge the next 5 creators.

title: Babel Tables for Multilingual Community Programs
one_liner: A tabletop translation hub that lets a senior-center lunch, ESL class or church group hold one conversation across four languages in real time.
customer: Senior centers, Area Agencies on Aging, libraries, faith groups and community colleges in multilingual cities, paying $150-300 a month per site plus hardware, funded from language-access and aging-services budgets.
problem: More than 25 million Americans have limited English proficiency, and isolated immigrant elders sit in language-siloed programs or nowhere. Interpreters cost $60-120 an hour, so programming stays segregated by language, blocking intergenerational and cross-cultural ties. Asian adults were the only Pew group net positive on chatbots for loneliness (37% help, 25% hurt), which signals openness to tech-mediated connection.
solution: A 4-microphone puck plus tablet that separates speakers and streams speech-to-speech translation to earbuds or phones, and captions on a table screen, for up to four languages at once. 'Table mode' runs low-stakes conversation card games, 'host mode' supports classes. Audio is processed ephemerally, with a human interpreter fallback for high-stakes moments.
why_now: Speech-to-speech translation reached conversational latency and usable quality in 2025 (translation in earbuds and meeting platforms), and small on-device models make private processing possible. State and city language-access mandates persist. Loneliness is a WHO-measured metric.
revenue_model: Hardware plus per-site SaaS, per-language add-ons, and contracts with city aging departments and Area Agencies on Aging.
non_obvious_insight: Translation tech was sold as an accommodation for one person and one interpreter. The bigger use is mixing: making the group itself multilingual so a Cantonese widow, a Spanish-speaking teen volunteer and an English-speaking regular can share one table. The unit of value is the table, not the user.
first_30_days: Prototype with a $200 speakerphone and a phone app. Pilot 'Table Tuesdays' in two senior centers (Chinese, Spanish, English) through a city aging department. Collect participation data over four weeks and charge $99 a month.

title: GLP-1 Off-Ramp Program for Cash-Pay Prescribers
one_liner: A structured 12-week landing program for people stopping GLP-1 drugs, sold to the prescribers who lose revenue the day a patient quits.
customer: Independent obesity-medicine clinics, med spas and cash-pay telehealth prescribers (pay per enrollee); secondary: patients paying $149-249 for the program.
problem: Every fitness and nutrition company is building for people ON the drug. But real-world data suggest up to roughly 65 percent quit within a year, and a 2026 meta-regression finds about 60 percent of lost weight returns within a year of stopping (individual studies vary). The discontinuation moment is unowned: prescribers lose the patient, gyms never see them, and regain triggers shame and churn.
solution: A program keyed to the last-dose date: taper coordination with the prescriber, protein and resistance-training progression, weekly connected-scale weigh-ins, human coach check-ins on hunger and food noise, and pre-agreed re-start triggers (for example +3 percent regain) that route the patient back to the prescriber. Delivered by app plus partner gyms.
why_now: Oral GLP-1s at $149-299 cash (Wegovy pill launched Dec 2025/Jan 2026, orforglipron in April 2026) make starting cheap and stopping easy; about 1 in 8 US adults report currently taking one; cash-pay churn is the biggest leak in prescriber P&Ls.
revenue_model: $150-300 per enrollee paid by the prescriber as a retention and win-back tool (or $199 patient-paid), plus a revenue share on patients who restart therapy.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is the prescriber, not the patient: the off-ramp is a retention product for the clinic's P&L, and a regain alert doubles as a win-back lead. Evidence on who regains is mixed, so a regain-risk model built from your own cohort becomes the proprietary asset.
first_30_days: Sign 3-5 independent clinics or med spas, enroll 30 patients ending therapy using an off-the-shelf connected scale, messaging tool and a lifting template, and track 90-day weight, lean-mass proxy and restart rate versus each clinic's history to use as the sales proof.

title: Belonging Pods to Cut Home-Care Aide Turnover
one_liner: Weekly peer pods and buddy mentors for isolated home-care aides, sold to agencies as a turnover-reduction service priced per retained aide.
customer: Home-care agencies (tens of thousands in the US, 50-500 aides each) and the Medicaid managed-care and Medicare Advantage plans that fund them, paying $8-15 per aide per month.
problem: Aides work alone in strangers' homes, with annual turnover often 65-80% and a replacement cost of several thousand dollars each. Engagement surveys measure isolation but fix nothing. Clients die and aides grieve without support. The workforce hired to cure elder loneliness is itself lonely, and agencies experience the pain only as attrition.
solution: Pods of 6 aides grouped by geography and shift, with a weekly 30-minute voice huddle (dial-in works, no app needed), a paid peer mentor per 30 aides, a monthly in-person meal, a 'hard visit' debrief line, and scripts for client death. A dashboard shows pod attendance against 90-day retention for the agency.
why_now: The aide shortage is acute. Immigration enforcement in 2025-26 is reported to be thinning a workforce in which roughly a quarter are immigrants. Plans and agencies want cheap retention levers, and loneliness is now legitimized as a health metric.
revenue_model: Per-aide monthly subscription with a performance kicker tied to retention, plus facilitator staffing margin. Later contracts with managed-care plans.
non_obvious_insight: Agencies do not buy belonging, they buy retention. Framing belonging as a turnover product with a hard ROI (each retained aide saves thousands) unlocks a budget that wellness and loneliness framing never will.
first_30_days: Sign three agencies with 100+ aides through state home-care association chapters. Run pods for about 60 aides and compare 90-day retention against a control group. Charge $6 per aide per month for the pilot.
